chunks: Ya'qub ibn 'Uthaym asked Abā 'Abdillāh عليه السلام and said to him:
A well of water has an odor in its water, and pieces of skin come out of it.
He said: “It is nothing, because the lizard may sometimes cast off its skin. For that, one bucket is sufficient for you.”

key_terms.الْوَزَغَ: a lizard, mentioned here as shedding its skin
key_terms.بِئْرُ: a well used as a source of water
key_terms.جِلْدَهُ: its skin, which may be the source of what is found in the water
key_terms.دَلْوٌ وَاحِدٌ: one bucket, the amount sufficient to draw out
key_terms.رِيحٌ: an odor or smell present in the water
key_terms.قِطَعُ جُلُودٍ: pieces of skin found coming out of the well

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on well water if it smells and pieces of skin are found in it?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a fiqh ruling regarding a well in which an odor and pieces of skin are found. Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام explains that this does not render the water problematic, as such skin may be from a lizard shedding, and removing a single bucket is sufficient.
